newsitem.title: JAPAN: Forex movements rapid, Japan watching closely - MOF.
newsitem.headline: Forex movements rapid, Japan watching closely - MOF.

text.p: Movements in foreign exchange markets are currently rather rapid and Japan will keep close watch on them, Kosuke Nakahira, special adviser to the Ministry of Finance, told Reuters on Wednesday.

"The condition of the (foreign exchange) market is not so abnormal compared to two years ago, but the movements are starting to gain speed. Monetary authorities of the G7 nations must keep careful watch over this," Nakahira said.
He explained that rapid movements in the market tend to invite active buying and selling, which further exacerbates the situation and causes the market to deviate from economic fundamentals.
"I don't think such a thing is happening now, but the pace is rather rapid. We must carefully watch this," Nakahira said.

Nakahira said that should the market's stability and credibility weaken from rapid movements which deviate from economic fundamentals, the Group of Seven (G7) nations should take appropriate action either by sounding out the market or taking action in the currency market.

"Monetary authorities of the G7 nations are keeping in close contact, especially when the markets are moving. It is the role of G7 nations to take steps when necessary by keeping in close contact, analysing data and exchanging views," he said.

The orderly reversal of the dollar since a G7 agreement in April 1995 has confirmed the G7 nations' vital role in the stabilisation of the currency market and contributed to global economic growth, he said.

"I would say that the overall trend of the currency market has generally reflected economic fundamentals. What we need now is to keep careful watch over whether market movements, which are rather rapid now, will deviate from economic fundamentals," Nakahira said.
He added that it was important to look not only at the dollar/yen rate, but also at moves in other major currencies.
